job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

passage: In the village of Rampur, farmers are shifting their practices to improve food security. Ramesh, a small-scale farmer, recently learned that primitive subsistence farming is not limited to remote tribes but is practiced by many small landholders using simple tools. He previously believed that adding excessive chemical fertilizers would increase his yield indefinitely, but agricultural experts warned him that soil health degrades if nutrients are not balanced. To manage his finances, Ramesh now relies on the Minimum Support Price (MSP), which is the guaranteed rate at which the government purchases crops from farmers to protect them from market fluctuations. This is distinct from the subsidized prices offered at ration shops for the poor. Furthermore, Ramesh has adjusted his planting schedule to match the seasons. He now sows wheat during the winter months, as it is a Rabi crop that requires cooler weather for germination, rather than planting it in the scorching summer heat. By understanding these scientific and institutional frameworks, the farmers of Rampur are ensuring a more sustainable future for their community. They are moving away from traditional myths and adopting methods that align with modern agricultural guidelines, ensuring that their land remains productive for generations to come.

items.evidence: He previously believed that adding excessive chemical fertilizers would increase his yield indefinitely, but agricultural experts warned him that soil health degrades if nutrients are not balanced.
items.q: Ramesh keeps adding more and more fertilizer to his field. What will most likely happen to the soil?
options: Its health will fall as nutrients get unbalanced
Its yield will keep rising every single year
Its nutrients will stay balanced by themselves
Its crops will grow better without any water
items.explain: Experts warned that soil health degrades when nutrients are not balanced, so excess fertilizer does not raise yield forever.

wrong.why: thinks more fertilizer always means higher yield
assumes soil fixes its own nutrient balance
thinks inputs like irrigation are not needed

items.evidence: To manage his finances, Ramesh now relies on the Minimum Support Price (MSP), which is the guaranteed rate at which the government purchases crops from farmers to protect them from market fluctuations.
items.q: Why does the MSP help Ramesh when market prices suddenly fall?
options: The government still buys his crop at a fixed rate
The government sells him cheap food at ration shops
The government gives him free land to grow more
The government takes his crop and pays him later
items.explain: MSP is a guaranteed rate at which the government buys crops, protecting farmers from market price changes.

wrong.why: thinks MSP is the price for selling food to the poor
thinks the government takes or gives land
invents a delayed payment not in the passage

items.evidence: Ramesh, a small-scale farmer, recently learned that primitive subsistence farming is not limited to remote tribes but is practiced by many small landholders using simple tools.
items.q: Which person shows that primitive subsistence farming is not limited to remote tribes?
options: A small landholder farming with simple tools
A tribal farmer burning a forest patch
A rich owner farming with many machines
A trader buying crops to sell abroad
items.explain: Many small landholders using simple tools also practise primitive subsistence farming, not only remote tribes.

wrong.why: links primitive farming only to slash and burn by tribes
confuses subsistence farming with machine-based commercial farming
mixes it up with commercial farming for sale

items.evidence: He now sows wheat during the winter months, as it is a Rabi crop that requires cooler weather for germination, rather than planting it in the scorching summer heat.
items.q: Why does Ramesh sow wheat in winter rather than in summer?
options: Wheat needs cool weather to sprout well
Wheat needs strong heat to sprout well
Wheat needs monsoon rain to sprout well
Wheat needs ration shops to sprout well
items.explain: Wheat is a Rabi crop that needs cooler weather for germination, so winter suits it better than summer.

wrong.why: thinks Rabi crops need a lot of heat
mixes Rabi with the monsoon Kharif season
picks a nearby unrelated detail from the passage
